behaviorChanges: Moving a provider-backed item to a done status now reads the linked issue's body and, when that issue carries an acceptance-criteria section, checks the posted verification evidence for a line-by-line AC pass/fail table with one row matched to each criterion. Matching is injective, so duplicate or paraphrased rows cannot cover distinct criteria, and a DEFERRED/PARTIAL/N-A verdict is not a row. A FAIL row is a FAILED AC, never a deferral, and no ordering of rows or of matching stages can hide one. The check runs as a PRE-FLIGHT, before any `gh project item-edit`, evidence comment, or UI-proof comment, so a refused done move mutates nothing. Governed by backlogProvider.doneEvidence.acTable, DEFAULT `warn`: the finding is printed as `done_evidence_ac_warning:` and the move proceeds.

`goal-advance` accepts --verification-evidence, --verification-evidence-file and --verification-evidence-url, composed through the same `backlog_provider_done_evidence_text` helper the other two done verbs already use, so file reading and URL validation keep one definition. A supplied AC table supersedes a stale AC table already recorded in the milestone's validationEvidence, because a FAIL row anywhere in the evidence fails its criterion and an appended correction would leave the stale FAIL refusing the closure it was meant to unblock. Before this release the primary autonomous closure path had no operator evidence channel at all, and with none supplied the composed evidence is byte-identical to previous releases.

New verb `tautline ac-verify --item <ref>` prints the AC table skeleton from the item's own written criteria, optionally writing it with --out. It derives the skeleton from the same splitter the gate uses, so the table a lane is told to produce is the table the gate accepts -- and the UNFILLED skeleton is refused, because a form that verifies itself is not verification.

A verification-CLAIMING comment posted through the CLI (a `## Verification` / `## Verification Evidence` heading, or a forbidden self-oracle phrase) is measured against the same criteria under the same knob. Comments that claim nothing about verification are neither fetched nor checked. NAMED RESIDUAL, not closed: a verification claim written into a PR body, a chat message or a delivery summary composed outside this CLI is not covered.

An unreadable issue body prints `done_evidence_ac_state: unknown` alongside the warning rather than degrading into a silent pass, so the fail-open rate is countable. PUBLISHED RATCHET CRITERIA for promoting the default to `strict`: at least 14 days of warn-mode records on a live board, a near-zero false-refusal rate with every observed false refusal fixed and pinned by a named regression test, an `unknown` rate low enough that the gate is measuring rather than skipping, and one demonstrated red -- a real done move correctly refused for a real unmet criterion. Promotion is an operator decision against those numbers, not a schedule.

KNOWN GAP, routed not fixed (tautline-backlog QUEUE item 95): a done move on a CROSS-REPO board item still posts its evidence comment to the LANE's repo. That predates this release -- stakeholder_issue_post_comment has always addressed data['repo'] -- but this release makes it visible, because the gate reads the criteria from the item's own repo. Same-repo items, the overwhelming majority, are unaffected.

optionalMigrations.description: backlogProvider.doneEvidence.acTable selects off|warn|strict for the closure-time AC-table gate. It defaults to warn, so no action is required to receive the finding; set it to off to skip the check and its issue-body read entirely, or to strict once the criteria below are met on your own board.

requiredMigrations.description: Run this FIRST. The hook's CLI path is baked by whichever install runs install-hooks, so reinstalling from an install that predates 0.49.0 rewrites the hook with the old resolver and reports success.

Then rewrite the hook FROM THE UPDATED CHECKOUT. The command is path-qualified on purpose: an unqualified `tautline` resolves from PATH, which may be the stale install this migration exists to route around, and run there it rewrites the hook with the OLD resolver and reports success. An adopter lane with no framework checkout uses `tautline install-hooks --target .`, which is safe there because the step above already updated the install that `tautline` resolves to. `lane-start` performs the same rewrite.

A board larger than the 5000-item read ceiling now REFUSES rather than silently returning a partial page. On 'board read truncated at N of M', narrow backlogProvider.scopeQuery so the read fits. Boards under the ceiling need no action.
Carried forward from 0.36.0: the declared Python floor is 3.12.
Carried forward from 0.38.0: testEvidence.enforcement defaults to `block`, and a lane with no tautline-test-run/v1 record classifies `missing`.
methodology-status --fail-on-drift requires the fleet-guard-hook PreToolUse entry. Carried forward from 0.17.0; lane-start also repairs it.

requiredMigrations.command: gh auth refresh --hostname github.com -s read:project -s project
requiredMigrations.description: Carried forward from 0.10.3 for lanes updating across it: grant the gh token the GitHub Projects scopes the fail-closed board gates need.

rollbackNotes: Repinning below 0.56.0 removes the closure gate, the `ac-verify` verb and the goal-advance evidence flags. No state migration in either direction: the adapter key is additive and older validators ignore it, and evidence posted under 0.56.0 is an ordinary issue comment.
WIP-safe: the gate ships at `warn`, so a lane that upgrades mid-flight is informed, not blocked.
